question: to the Council Letizia Moratti (PPE), Massimiliano Salini (PPE), Flavio Tosi (PPE), Caterina Chinnici (PPE), Salvatore De Meo (PPE), Giusi Princi (PPE), Fulvio Martusciello (PPE), Marco Falcone (PPE) Subject:

The Ceuta migrant crisis has brought a number of key issues to the fore, namely the management of irregular migrant flows, the security of Europe’s external borders and the functioning of the Schengen system. Press reports indicate that the Spanish Audiencia Nacional is verifying whether any people with links to jihadist terrorism – including extremists who are known to the authorities and individuals who have previously been deported for their radical inclinations – have crossed the border into Spain. The Ceuta migration crisis is clear proof that uncontrolled flows can facilitate the entry of people who pose a security risk. One cannot rule out the involvement of criminal networks or the possibility that external actors could be weaponising these migration flows. In this regard, any uncertainty or grey area in the management of migrant flows could cause issues not just for the two countries involved, but for Europe as a whole. As a result, Europe needs to test how effective the Entry/Exist system (which recently became fully operational) and the EU’s other border management tools are in emergency situations. In the light of the above, we ask the Council: 1.

Does it know whether any high-risk individuals have managed to enter the EU through Ceuta, and could it specify the nature of the checks that have been carried out by Europol, the SIS, Interpol and national authorities?

What measures will be taken to promptly step up border identification and screening procedures and bolster database interoperability with a view to preventing any breaches in the Schengen security architecture?

What urgent steps will be taken to introduce stricter conditions in the EU’s agreements with third countries with a view to supporting the Member States exposed to these migration flows and preventing the latter from being used as a geopolitical tool?
